chapter: After Cab: Don Redman, teaching and records
title: Art Tatum in Toledo and at the Cotton Club
summary: Thomas recalls hearing Tatum in a Toledo alley restaurant, getting him to play the Cotton Club, and Tatum's card tricks.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: There's another guy that... I've always admired great musicians.
Well, you're a great musician yourself.
There's one guy in Toledo, Ohio; I'll never forget it. We used to go in that alley...
Are you talking about Art Tatum?

I have never in my life heard nobody play... And he ruined a lot of piano players. Because he sounded like two piano players when he played. And he finally came to New York, and we talked him into coming to the Cotton Club. Because we got to be friendly... I think he was in the band when we used to go in that little alley back there in Toledo and eat...
When (?) to come in the Cotton Club, would he play there?
Yeah, he came up one night, and he played. Because we knew how great he was. We introduced him and begged him to get up and play a song.
And he was such a nice guy, too. He could gamble. He could play cards. He'd get the cards and put them... He didn't see too good, but he could see a little bit. He'd get the cards...
I was working with him when I joined the band.
Oh yeah? Then you knew him.
Yeah, I knew him. I was at the Three Deuces with him, when Cab... I used to play pinochle with him every night.
Yeah, and he'd put them cards up there...
After he saw them cards, he knew every one in there.
